name: PostHog Analytics
description: Read your pod's product analytics out of PostHog: event counts over time, unique users, the top events, and per-step reach. This is the READ half of the self-hosted PostHog project — the client apps already send events in (the `phc_…` project token is INGEST-ONLY), and this capability answers questions about what arrived. It installs ONE `vault://` tool whose `baseUrl` pins the PostHog host AND the project id at install time, so no caller (human or AI) can point the credential at another org's project or pass arbitrary HogQL — the verbs are a small fixed program of named reads. PRECONDITION: a PostHog PERSONAL API KEY with query:read (plus insight:read/event:read/person:read) — NOT the `phc_…` project token, which always 401s on a read. The capability fails loudly when the key is absent or invalid; it never reports a broken lookup as an empty dashboard.

params.name: personalApiKey
params.label: PostHog Personal API Key
params.description: A PostHog PERSONAL API KEY (PostHog → Settings → Personal API keys) with query:read, insight:read, event:read and person:read scopes. Stored server-encrypted in the pod vault as a pod-wide secret; never persisted in this template. The `phc_…` project token used by the client apps is INGEST-ONLY and will be rejected by every read.

params.name: projectId
params.label: PostHog project id
params.description: The numeric PostHog project id whose analytics belong to THIS pod (2 for the Synap org). It is baked into the installed tool's baseUrl and is deliberately NOT a call parameter, so no verb can ever read a different project.

params.name: analyticsHost
params.label: PostHog host
params.description: Origin of the PostHog instance, e.g. https://analytics.synap.live (self-hosted) or https://us.posthog.com (PostHog Cloud). Baked into the installed tool's baseUrl at install time.

vault.name: {{name}} PostHog Personal API Key
vault.description: PostHog Personal API Key, read scopes only. Pod-wide: the analytics belong to the pod, so every pod member and every agent reads the same project through this one secret.

tools.name: posthog_api
tools.description: Authenticated read access to the pod's PostHog project. `config.baseUrl` pins host + project id at install time; `config.auth` injects the vaulted Personal API Key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Nothing outside this capability should execute it directly.

skills.name: posthog.event_trend
skills.description: READ: how often ONE named event happened over time (PostHog insights/trend, math=total). Use it for "how many signups this week", "is feature X being used", "did the deploy verification events arrive". Read-only: auto-runs, no approval. Args: { event: string (the PostHog event name, e.g. "$pageview", "synap_deploy_verified"), days?: 1-90 (default 7), interval?: "hour"|"day"|"week" (default day) }. Returns { event, window, metric, series: [{ label, count, labels, data }], seriesCount, empty } — `empty: true` means the query RAN and the window held no matching event; a failure throws instead.

event.description: The PostHog event name to count, e.g. "$pageview" or "synap_deploy_verified".

skills.name: posthog.unique_users
skills.description: READ: unique people over time (PostHog insights/trend, math=dau). Use it for "how many active users do we have", "is anyone coming back". Read-only: auto-runs. Args: { event?: string (default "$pageview"), days?: 1-90 (default 7), interval?: "day"|"week" (default day) }. Returns the same shape as posthog.event_trend with metric "unique_users".

event.description: The event that counts as activity (default "$pageview").

skills.name: posthog.top_events
skills.description: READ: which events fired most in the window, highest volume first. Use it as the FIRST question — "what is actually happening in my product" — before naming a specific event. Read-only: auto-runs. Args: { days?: 1-90 (default 7), limit?: 1-100 (default 10) }. Returns { columns, rows: [{ event, event_count }], rowCount, empty }. The query is a fixed HogQL program (the event name is never caller-supplied here); `empty: true` means events exist nowhere in the window, and a failure throws instead.

skills.name: posthog.step_reach
skills.description: READ: how many unique people performed EACH of an ordered list of events anywhere in the window. This is step REACH, not a funnel conversion rate — it does not claim the steps happened in order, because an ordered funnel (windowFunnel / the funnel insight endpoint) could not be verified against a live instance yet, and a guessed aggregate would read as a calm zero. Read-only: auto-runs. Args: { steps: string[] (2-8 PostHog event names, in the order you care about), days?: 1-90 (default 7) }. Returns { steps: [{ step, event, users }], empty }. If you need a true conversion rate, say so explicitly rather than interpreting `users` as one.

steps.description: 2-8 PostHog event names, in the order you care about.
